changes_before_any_run.change: The one-step error behind residual evidence (the primary signal for Q2) is now the critic's own training form: the target averages min_h Q(s', clip(c(s') + noise, -1, 1)) over 32 fixed draws of td3_bc_update's training noise (normal, standard deviation 0.2, clipped at 0.5), as BCA's own residual and the critic's training target do; draw d of log row i is row i of default_rng([20261015, seed, 94, d + 1]).standard_normal((log rows, 4)), so a row gets the same draws in both worlds and at every share. The noiseless form (spec v1) is kept as the reported signal residual_evidence_noiseless. The gap between the two, 0.98 J(s'), is reported at the training rows by region and command (J-by-region diagnostic, both worlds, beside the readout and in the pooled look) and at every pair (neighbour_offset). On T1 and T1c every signal is also read relative to the row's recorded command at the same state (score(s, a) - score(s, a_i), the A1 form), reported; the flag-based Q2 is unchanged.

changes_before_any_run.reason: The offset is not a constant that the T4 flag level cancels. With noise draws at seed 0 (32 draws, seed-0 check h and verify/v1_offset_pairs.py; the reviewer's 16 draws agree), J at the next states of the gapped log's training rows is, region rows against the rest: stalling world, full-log critic (has learned the stall) +0.270 / +0.132; no-stall world, full-log critic +0.124 / +0.113; gapped critics +0.133 / +0.113 (stalling) and +0.128 / +0.113 (no-stall). In the region the stall-aware controller sits at its 80% cap, so the training noise reaches past-80% commands, which a critic that has learned the stall drops. A trace critic that learns the stall would therefore get up to about +0.14 more offset at region rows in the stalling world only, lowering residual evidence there: against the separation Q2 looks for, and about the size of the trace signal the plan cites (-0.10 against +0.12). T4 is 84% outside the region (region share 15.7% stalling, 15.4% no-stall), so its level cannot remove it. In the training form a well-fitted row has an error near 0 whatever the critic's shape at s'.

detection.actor: the trace critic's actor of the log (share 0: check 2's gapped-critic actor); the critic, clone and training rows are the log's own
detection.definitions:
EXPLORATORY trace test bed: the detection readout with data-only stand-ins (plan sections 4.4 and 4.6). NO BCA:
no band, calibrator, threshold, dose or BCA update is called; every score here is a stand-in computed from the log,
the frozen fixed-controller critic and the cloned actor. The detect component of Stage 1 was not ready when this was
written (scratchpad/ood/detect/ did not exist), so these are this test bed's own implementations, written to the
plan's definitions.

One-step error at training row i, with the log's frozen critic (spec v2, review finding 1): the critic's own training
form,
  delta_i = r_i + 0.98 (1 - done_i) * mean_d min_h Q_h(s'_i, clip(c(s'_i) + eps_id, -1, 1)) - min_h Q_h(s_i, a_i),
recorded r_i and s'_i, c the stall-aware controller as the critic's target reads it (learners.FixedController on the
normalised next observation), eps_id = clip(0.2 z_id, -0.5, 0.5) with z_id standard normal: the training noise of
td3_bc_update (policy noise 0.2, clipped at 0.5, then the command clipped to +-1), averaged over 32 fixed draws.
Draw d of log row i is row i of default_rng([20261015, seed, 94, d + 1]).standard_normal((log rows, 4)), so a row
gets the same draws in both worlds and at every share. The critic was trained toward exactly this target (its
target copy in place of its final parameters), so at a well-fitted row delta is about 0 whatever the critic's shape
along the command at s'.
Why not the noiseless next command (spec v1, the room test's form): then delta_noiseless_i = delta_i + 0.98 J(s'_i),
J(s') = min_h Q(s', c(s')) - mean_d min_h Q(s', clip(c(s') + eps_d)). J is not a constant: at seed 0 it is +0.27 at
region rows against +0.13 elsewhere for a critic that has learned the stall (the full-log critic, stalling world)
and +0.12 / +0.11 in the no-stall world, because where the stall-aware controller sits at its 80% cap the noise
reaches past-80% commands, whose value a stall-aware critic drops. That offset lowers residual evidence at region
rows in the stalling world only, against the separation Q2 looks for, and T4 (84% outside the region) cannot cancel
it. The noiseless form is kept as a reported signal (residual_evidence_noiseless); 0.98 (1 - done) J is reported per
row group and at every pair (neighbour_offset): the J-by-region diagnostic of both worlds.

Stand-ins, each a score at a (state, command) pair (s, a); larger means "more suspect":
  residual_evidence  PRIMARY. Minus the mean one-step error (training form, above) of the 10 nearest training rows of
                     the log, in standardised (state, command) space (the gate's distance-to-data space:
                     shift.card_reference's columns, standardised by the log's kept training rows). A critic that
                     overrates the commands near (s, a) leaves negative errors there, so the score is high.
  residual_evidence_noiseless  reported: the same with the noiseless next command (spec v1's form).
  distance           the distance to the 10th-nearest training row in the same space (the gate's distance to data).
  range_hinge        sum_j ([a_j - hi_j]_+^2 + [lo_j - a_j]_+^2), lo_j and hi_j the 0.5% and 99.5% quantiles of the
                     log's training commands per thruster (the recorded range; the data-only rival with no signal).
  density            behaviour density: 1/2 sum_k ((a_k - c_k(s)) / sigma_k)^2, c the log's cloned actor, sigma_k the
                     maximum-likelihood spread (root mean square of a_ik - c_k(s_i) over the log's training rows).
  heads              two-head disagreement |Q1 - Q2|(s, a) of the log's frozen critic.
Also at every pair, reported: neighbour_offset (the mean of 0.98 (1 - done) J over the same 10 nearest rows; the
noiseless score is residual_evidence - neighbour_offset exactly) and neighbour_past80 (a past-80% training row among
the 10 nearest: does the trace reach the pair at all?).

Flag level: the ceil((n + 1) * 0.95)-th smallest score on T4 (split-conformal 95% level). A pair is flagged when
its score is above the level.

Pair sets (fixed before any run; spec.json):
  T1   1,500 full-throttle-region training states, PAIRED across worlds (spec v2): log rows that are kept training
       rows in the region in BOTH worlds' gapped logs (so kept in every trace log), chosen by
       default_rng([20261015, seed, 92]); the same log positions in both worlds (the state at a position can differ
       between the worlds). At each, the log's trace critic's actor's command and that command capped at 80%. Primary set.
       Also scored at the row's recorded command a_i (re-referencing, reported: score(s, a) - score(s, a_i)).
  T1c  the T1 states at a command common to both worlds: check 1's full-throttle pattern (recorder.pattern, float32)
       and the same pattern capped at 80% (check 1's c_hi and c_cap). Every pair is past 80%. Reported: unlike T1,
       its past-80% pairs are not selected by what each world's critic taught its actor.
  T3a  1,500 strong-current states visited by the trace critic's actor (exact rollouts from the first 200 starts of
       the strong-current bank, 100 steps each), chosen by default_rng([20261015, seed, 93, world index, 0]); the
       actor's command and its cap. Reported.
  T3b  the same with states visited by the stall-aware controller (default_rng([.., 93, world index, 1])). Reported.
  T4   5,000 held-out recorded rows: the evaluation split outside the gap ball, chosen by
       default_rng([20261012, seed, 77]) (the fallback diagnostic's check rows), at their recorded commands. Sets the
       flag levels; never trained on.
Past-80% pairs: pairs whose command is past 80% on any thruster (thruster_chain.past_knee).
Per set and signal: the flag rate at past-80% pairs (the selectivity's input), at their 80% caps, at the other
pairs; paired widening (the share of past-80% pairs whose score at the command exceeds the score at the cap); on T1
and T1c the re-referenced score at past-80% pairs (mean of score(s, a) - score(s, a_i), and the share above 0).
Selectivity (run_job.py, pooled phase): the flag rate at past-80% pairs in the stalling world minus the same in the
no-stall world, per seed, share, set and signal; a world with fewer than 20 past-80% pairs in a set gives no value.
detection.detect_component: the Stage 1 detect component (scratchpad/ood/detect/) did not exist when this spec was written, so these are this test bed's own implementations of the plan's definitions. If its locked signals become available they may be added as reported extras under a new spec version; they never replace the primary signal or set
detection.offset_diagnostic: J(s') = min_h Q(s', c(s')) - mean over the draws of min_h Q(s', clip(c(s') + noise)) at the training rows' next states, summarised for region rows, the rest and past-80% rows; neighbour_offset = the mean of 0.98 (1 - done) J over a pair's 10 nearest rows. Reported in every readout and per seed and world in the pooled look

one_step_error.critic: the frozen critic's final parameters on both sides (training used a slowly moving target copy for the target)
one_step_error.heads: min over the two heads on both sides

detection.selectivity: flag rate at past-80% pairs in the stalling world minus the same in the no-stall world, per seed, share, set and signal; no value when either world has fewer than 20 past-80% pairs in the set

deviations: The gate's functions are called unchanged instead of a re-typed copy of the critic and actor protocols (plan 4.6: 'scripts import the gate's code read-only'). The protocol and its settings are the gate's by construction.

Normalisation is the gate's (the gapped log's kept rows), not recomputed on each trace log: the gate uses it for every critic of a seed, and the reused critics need it. The trace rows change it by a few parts in ten thousand at most.

The cloned actor and the full-log critic's actor are retrained on each trace log; only the critics are reused. They cannot be identical to the gate's, because the clone's rows and the actor row stream depend on the log's rows. Share 0 reuses everything from the gate.
Added reported arm: the gate's gapped critic's actor trained on the trace log. trace - gapped separates the effect of the critic's data from the change of start actor and row stream.
The 0.5% rows are a subset of the 2% rows (one permutation per seed and world), so the two shares form a dose ladder.
The calibration bank gets the same add-back rule. Nothing here reads it; a later BCA test would.

The plan leaves the pair sets and the primary set of the selectivity open. They are fixed here: T1 (region training states, where the actor learns the belief and where a training-time penalty acts) is primary; T3a and T3b (strong current) are reported.
Flag levels come from 5,000 held-out evaluation-split rows outside the gap ball (the fallback diagnostic's check rows), so the levels describe recorded data like the training data.

Residual evidence's one-step error uses the minimum over the critic's two heads on both sides and the critic's training form of the target: the controller's next command plus the training noise, averaged over 32 fixed draws, with the recorded reward and next state (spec v2, change R1). The noiseless form (spec v1, the room test's form) is reported as residual_evidence_noiseless; the offset between them is reported by region in both worlds.
The trace rows and the T1 states are the same log positions in both worlds (spec v2, change R3); the common-command set T1c and the re-referenced scores on T1 and T1c are reported additions.
Every computing phase runs pinned to one CPU (spec v2, change R2).
The questions are judged on the mean over seeds 0-2; each seed is reported.
The trace critic's overrating is read on check 1's frozen region pool with check 1's saved exact values (no new simulation).
Harm in the no-stall world (where pushing past 80% helps) is reported, not judged.
The detect component's signals were not ready; own implementations of residual evidence, distance to data, the range hinge, behaviour density and two-head disagreement are used.
Compute is projected from the measured seed-0 timing instead of the plan's 30 process-hours.
evaluation: acceptance._evaluate (learners.evaluate_actor): exact 100-step returns on the full 1,000-start banks of the four situations (recorded conditions, strong current, big waves, big kicks), points against the gate's anchors of the world (0 = recording controller, 100 = stall-aware controller), the same actor capped at 80%, the share of steps past 80%. Actors: the trace log's cloned actor and the trace, full and gapped arms. harm = points(full) - points(trace), per situation
label: EXPLORATORY: trace test bed (plan section 4.6), computed outside the gate on saved gate artifacts and new trace logs; not a gated output; changes no pre-registered rule; no BCA band, calibrator, threshold, dose, BCA update or BCA training arm was used (data-only stand-ins only)

purpose: The harm claim, 'BCA identifies the harm itself, not just novelty', needs data that carry a trace of the harm. The gate's gapped log keeps only 34-59 rows past 80% throttle (about 0.1%), so nothing in it can tell a harmful unsupported command from a merely unrecorded one. A trace log keeps a small, seeded, random share of the rows the gate's removal took out past 80%: 0.5% and 2% of them. This test bed builds those logs in both worlds for gate seeds 0-2, retrains the fixed-controller critic and check 2's actors on them, and asks whether the harm survives and whether a data-only residual signal can then tell the two worlds apart. It runs no part of BCA. If both answers are yes, these logs become the test bed for a later harm claim under its own pre-registration (plan 4.6).

questions.Q1: Does the trace critic still overrate pushing past 80%, with harm of at least 50 points in strong current? Yes when the mean over seeds 0-2 of harm = points(full-log critic's actor) - points(trace critic's actor) in strong current, stalling world, is at least 50 (every seed needed). The pull past 80% is reported beside it
questions.Q2: Does residual evidence separate the two worlds with selectivity of at least 0.2, where the range hinge cannot? Yes when, on T1, the mean over seeds 0-2 of residual evidence's selectivity (training-form one-step error) is at least 0.2 and the range hinge's is below 0.2 (every seed needed). Reported, not judged: the other stand-ins (the noiseless residual evidence among them), the other sets (T1c, the common command, among them), the re-referenced differences on T1 and T1c, and the J-by-region diagnostic of both worlds
questions.missing: a stopped or failed job, or a world with too few past-80% pairs, gives no value for that seed, and a mean that needs it gives no answer (the question is then not answered yes)
questions.reference: share 0 (the gate's gapped log) gets the same numbers, reported only
questions.verdict: per share: usable for a later harm claim when Q1 and Q2 are both yes. Exploratory: seeds 0-2 only; any claim needs its own pre-registration and fresh seeds

reuse.critics: the gate's full-log and gapped fixed-controller critics of the stall-aware controller, both worlds, read with acceptance.get_critic(..., train=False) (SHA-256 checked); identical for every share, so never retrained
reuse.not_reused: the cloned actor and the full-log critic's actor are retrained on each trace log: they are not identical to the gate's (the clone's rows and the actor-only row stream depend on the log's rows)
reuse.reference: share 0 is the gate's own gapped log: nothing is trained. Check 2's saved cloned, gapped-critic and full-log-critic actors and their saved points, check 1's saved pull past 80%, the gate's gapped critic and saved clone are read back (SHA-256 checked); only the detection readout is computed

room_spec.lesson: change A1: a penalty must be read relative to the recorded command at the same state; the noiseless one-step error carries an offset (about +0.15 at recorded commands) that depends on the state and on the command, not a constant. This test bed trains no penalty. Its residual evidence uses the critic's training form (noise-averaged target), so the offset does not enter it; the offset is reported by region in both worlds; and on T1 and T1c every score is also read relative to the row's recorded command (reported). Any later penalty on these logs must use the re-referenced form [delta*(s, a_i) - delta*(s, a)]_+.

spec_history.replaced_because: review of the trace test bed, before any training run: (R1, major) residual evidence's one-step error now uses the critic's training form (target averaged over 32 fixed draws of the training noise) instead of the noiseless next command, whose offset depends on the region and on what the critic learned about the stall; the noiseless form, the J-by-region diagnostic of both worlds and re-referenced scores on T1 and T1c are reported; (R2) every computing phase must run pinned to one CPU, with new seed-0 checks that the train phase's actor-only call reproduces check 2's actors and the critic protocol reproduces the gate's first chunk; (R3) the two worlds add back the same trace rows (one permutation per seed over the candidates both worlds share) and T1 uses the same positions in both worlds, with a common-command set T1c reported; (R4) launch.sh skips stopped jobs, survives a failed job and runs seeds side by side. No outcome of any trace job exists; the seed-0 build records, checks, timing and code of spec v1 move to superseded/v1

spec_history.kept: every key of spec v2 is kept in spec v3 unchanged, apart from 'version' and 'previous_spec'
spec_history.replaced_because: POST HOC: chosen after seeing the 0.5% and 2% results. The user asked for both claims ('do both'). Neither share planned in spec v2 is usable for a harm claim: at 0.5% kept the harm stayed (96.5 points in strong current) but residual evidence did not separate the two worlds (selectivity 0.076 on T1), and at 2% kept the harm stayed (85.8 points) and the worlds were again not separated (0.071). Spec v3 adds the kept shares 1%, 3%, 5% and 10% with the same rule, the same permutation, the same critic and actor protocol, the same signals and the same questions and marks, to map whether any share from 0 to 10% leaves both a large harm (at least 50 points) and a detectable trace (selectivity at least 0.2), or whether the critic learns the stall before the trace becomes detectable. Spec v2 and its results are kept as they are, and nothing is chosen on the new results.

added rows unique, among the gate's removed training rows, all past 80%
